criteria.check: Read metrics.py compute(); every Metric value is produced by Python arithmetic over categorised transactions; llm.py providers only return prose. Enforcement that the memo contains no other figure depends on guard (see R4/P2).
Read every Metric(...) constructor in metrics.py; each carries evidence ids; tests/test_metrics.py::test_evidence_reproduces_each_figure passes. Note the CLI output does not carry the ids (finding).

Read graph.py draft(): user message is account name, period, metrics.as_table() (id, name, display value, method; no evidence or descriptions) and the policy rules. No transaction text reaches the model.

Read guard.py and graph.py routing; probed guard with adversarial memos. Redraft cap (2) and not-grounded flag to reviewer are correct, but the guard marks memos grounded that contain invented figures glued to letters (48250GBP) and sign-flipped money (overdraft stated as credit).

Read graph.py review()/finalise() and models.ReviewDecision; probed resume with reviewer='   ' and caller-supplied decided_at. interrupt gating works, but a blank reviewer and a backdated timestamp are accepted, and the decision is held only in an in-process MemorySaver (rejections are never persisted).
Read categorise.py: ordered RULES list, first direction-matching rule wins, unmatched credit falls through to Category.OTHER.
Read policy.py and policy/uk_sme_default.yaml: rules are YAML with op/threshold/on_fail and refer bands; outcomes pass/refer/fail. (No schema validation of on_fail: minor finding.)

Committed statements are generated by synth.py (examples/, evals/results/statements/); grep for sort codes, IBANs and email addresses in data dirs found none. Full provenance of every committed file outside the platform lens not proven.

Read ingest.load_csv: missing columns, empty file, empty/duplicate ids, bad dates, non-finite amounts/balances and running-balance breaks all collected and raised as StatementError; CLI maps it to exit 2. tests/test_ingest.py passes.
Read .github/workflows/ci.yml: installs .[dev,mcp] (no llm extra), runs ruff, pytest and evals with --llm fake; no secrets referenced. Ran pytest locally: 94 passed.

Probe: 675 synth statements (seeds 1-25 x months 6/12/18 x 9 cases) compared M2,M5,M6,M7,M8,M11,M12 to truth. 3 mismatches, all M5 (trades/good seeds 1,6,9, 12 months): metric 17327.55 / 16704.74 / 16356.30 vs truth 14000.00 (the opening balance). CI only tests seed 7.
Probe: guard.check('DSCR 1.42 [M10]. Stock is worth 48250GBP.') returns grounded=True; same for GBP48250, 48250pounds, 3500GBP. Number regex lookarounds skip any number touching a letter.

findings.claim: The NUMBER regex requires no letter immediately before (line 25) or after (line 29) a number, so any figure written against a currency code or word is never scanned. An invented amount written '48250GBP', 'GBP48250' or '48250pounds' passes as grounded, and --yes will approve it.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from cma import guard; from cma.models import Metric; M=[Metric(id='M10',name='d',value=1.42,unit='ratio',method='x')]; print(guard.check('DSCR 1.42 [M10]. Stock is worth 48250GBP.',M).grounded)"  -> True

findings.claim: _matches accepts the written number against both +value and -value, so a memo that states an overdraft as a credit balance, or negative operating cash flow as positive, is grounded. Sign is the money fact for M5 and M9.
findings.repro: M5=-2300, M9=-15000: guard.check('The lowest balance was £2,300 [M5], so the account stayed in credit.') -> grounded True; guard.check('Net operating cash flow was £15,000 [M9].') -> grounded True (scratchpad panel02/platform/guard_probe.py).

findings.claim: M5 'Lowest balance' is the minimum post-transaction balance and ignores the opening balance (derivable as first.balance - first.amount). When the account starts at its low point the metric overstates the lowest balance by thousands, and P1 fails.
findings.repro: synth.generate('trades','good',seed=1,months=12,end=date(2026,9,30)) -> M5=17327.55, truth.lowest_balance=14000.00; also seeds 6 (16704.74) and 9 (16356.30). 3/675 cases in panel02/platform/p1.py. tests/test_metrics.py only exercises seed 7.

findings.claim: The draft prompt hands the model the policy rule descriptions and details ('Debt service cover of at least 1.25x', 'rule requires >= 1.25', '60', '-15'), and system rule 4 tells it to explain referred/failed rules, but thresholds are not metrics, so any memo that restates a threshold is ungrounded. A real model will hit this routinely: redraft loops and analysts trained to override the guard. Only FakeLLM, which never quotes thresholds, has been evaluated.
findings.repro: guard.check('Debt service cover of 1.42 [M10] is below the policy refer band of 1.5x and the 1.25x minimum.', M) -> unmatched ['1.5x','1.25x']; 'Top customer share is 38.0% [M15], under the 60% limit.' -> unmatched ['60%'].

findings.claim: DEFAULT_POLICY resolves to <site-packages parent>/policy/uk_sme_default.yaml, but the wheel (pyproject.toml:30 packages=['src/cma']) ships no policy file. Any non-editable install (pip install ., pip install git+..., a container image for the v0.2 Helm chart) fails at the policy node with FileNotFoundError unless --policy is passed.
findings.repro: pip wheel . --no-deps -> wheel contains only cma/*.py; extract it and run python3 -I -c 'from cma import policy; policy.load_policy()' -> FileNotFoundError .../policy/uk_sme_default.yaml

findings.claim: Review state lives only in an in-process MemorySaver, and nothing persists the human decision: a pending review is lost if the process dies, a rejection is printed and then discarded (cli.py:95), and checkpoints accumulate without bound in a long-running process. To run as a service it needs a durable checkpointer (Postgres/SQLite with the same serde allow-list) and an append-only decision log; today the only record is the --out file of an approved memo.
findings.repro: After one run, len(list(graph.checkpointer.list(cfg))) == 10, all in memory; cma run ... answering 'n' exits 1 with no file written and no decision stored anywhere.

findings.claim: The deliverable memo written with --out contains [Mn] tags but no metrics table, methods or evidence ids, and the console table prints only evidence counts (cli.py:125). A compliance reader holding the memo cannot trace a figure to statement lines without re-running the pipeline or the MCP server, which is the bet's stated problem.
findings.repro: cma run examples/cafe_stretched.csv --yes --reviewer A --out m.md; grep -c T0 m.md -> 0 (no transaction ids anywhere in the artefact).

findings.claim: reviewer min_length=1 accepts whitespace, and decided_at (line 134) is accepted from the resume payload, so an approval can be stamped 'APPROVED by     at 2020-01-01'. Reviewer identity is self-asserted text with no authentication, which a service will need.

The CLI defaults --llm to 'fake' and so ignores CMA_LLM, and the finalise stamp (graph.py:167) does not record the provider, model, policy name/hash or code version. A pilot user who forgets --llm gets the FakeLLM template memo (with its canned 'can proceed to approval' sentence), approved and stamped with nothing showing it was not model-drafted.
findings.repro: CMA_LLM=anthropic cma run examples/cafe_stretched.csv --yes --reviewer A -> FakeLLM memo, no API call; stamp has no model field.

findings.claim: Provider responses are not checked for stop_reason/finish_reason, and the guard does not check required headings, so a memo cut off at max_tokens=1500 (line 71) or before the Recommendation section passes as grounded. Provider exceptions are not caught (cli.py:57 catches only StatementError), so they surface as raw tracebacks, and there is no logging anywhere in src/ to show latency, retries or token use (Langfuse, the v0.2 tracing tool, has nothing to attach to).
findings.repro: guard.check('Revenue was £612,345 [M2] and DSCR 1.42 [M10].', M) -> grounded True with no Recommendation; grep -rn logging src/ -> no matches.

findings.claim: Tolerance scales with the written precision and ignores units, so coarse or unit-swapped figures are grounded: '£1m [M2]' for M2=£612,345, and '12x [M1]' (months stated as a ratio).
findings.repro: guard.check('Revenue was £1m [M2] over the year.', M) -> True; guard.check('Debt service cover was 12x [M1]', M) -> True.

findings.claim: MCP tools accept any filesystem path, and StatementError echoes the file's first line, so a client can probe arbitrary host files. This is harmless over local stdio but a disclosure risk once the server is exposed for v0.2. There is no allow-listed statement root.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from cma import mcp_server; mcp_server.statement_summary('/etc/passwd')" -> error text includes 'found: root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash'

findings.claim: The eval's truth check and exit code (line 72) cover only M2, yet ci.yml:22 and README:60 claim CI fails 'if any computed metric disagrees with ground truth'. The M5 defect above would not fail the eval.

Policy YAML is not validated: on_fail accepts 'pass', so a failed rule silently passes, and an unknown metric or op raises a bare KeyError mid-graph. A policy edit (the intended change path) can fail open without any error.
findings.repro: Edit a rule to on_fail: pass with an unmet threshold -> RuleOutcome.PASS; overall can become pass.
